incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty - Incident P-43921 triggered for service: internal-vpc-endpoints in us-west-2d (az-d). Symptoms: increased 5xx from control-plane calls, failed egress to S3/metadata, and a spike in NAT gateway connection churn.

Sam (oncall): I'm seeing alerts for 5xx on the model-pull job and a bunch of ENI detach/attach on instances in az-d. Paging into #incidents.

Priya (netops): Confirmed. Route table associations for private-subnet-azd are flapping. Also seeing a bunch of RoutePropagation changes for the AZD NAT TGW.

Nate (infra): Are customers reporting user-facing errors? Marta, any CS tickets?

Marta (support): Yes, 3 customers in EU reported timeouts hitting hosted inference endpoints that route through az-d. Impact seems intermittent but elevated for the last ~8m.

Sam (oncall): Triage plan: 1) Stop autoscaling in az-d to prevent noisy churn. 2) Move failover traffic to az-b/c via routing policy. 3) Investigate VPC route table changes and source.

Priya (netops): I'm looking at CloudTrail. I see a Terraform apply from a service account 1739456700 that modified a route table association to use a new ENI-based endpoint. That apply finished ~2m before alerts. Could be a bad rollout.

Nate (infra): Rolling the route change back now. Command:```bash
# revert route assoc
aws ec2 disassociate-route-table-association --association-id rtbassoc-0abc1234
# force re-assoc to original
aws ec2 associate-route-table --route-table-id rtb-0def5678 --subnet-id subnet-azd-private
```

Sam (oncall): Reverting. Also I'm setting service-level routing to avoid az-d for now:```json
{"route_policy": {"preferred_azs": ["az-a","az-b","az-c"], "exclude_azs": ["az-d"]}}
```

incident-bot: Update: Route table association revert completed at 1739457180.

Priya (netops): After revert, NAT gateway connection count stabilized but still seeing failed conntrack entries on instances created during the bad apply. Suspect conntrack table exhaustion on some NAT proxies.

Nate (infra): Spawning replacement NAT proxies in az-b and az-c and scaling down az-d proxies. Command used:```bash
# create new nat-proxy ASG in az-b
aws autoscaling update-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name nat-proxy-asg --min-size 3 --max-size 6 --desired-capacity 4 --availability-zones us-west-2b
```

Sam (oncall): Noting customer impact: partial timeouts for hosted API calls for customers pinned to az-d; most traffic now failing over to other AZs due to routing policy. Estimated affected requests 0.6% of total at peak.

Marta (support): Notified affected customers with a quick status note. ETA for full remediation?

Priya (netops): Need to clear conntrack on remaining NAT proxies in az-d. Plan: graceful drain + conntrack flush:```bash
# drain
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:tg:... --targets Id=i-0123
# conntrack flush (run on the NAT proxy before decommission)
sudo conntrack -F
```

Sam (oncall): Doing the drain on the last 2 nat-proxies in az-d.

incident-bot: PagerDuty - Incident P-43921 acknowledged by Sam at 1739456905.

Nate (infra): After drain and flush, I see 200s restored for model-pull jobs and S3 egress. CloudWatch: 5xx rate dropped back to baseline by 1739459000.

Priya (netops): Root cause: an automated rollout that swapped a subnet's route-table association to a new ENI-based service endpoint (dualstack config) which didn't have proper conntrack size settings; that change caused NAT proxies to hit conntrack limits and subsequent connection resets. Also the rollback script did not fully clear ephemeral associations causing route propagation churn.

Sam (oncall): Mitigation summary: 1) Rolled back route-table assoc. 2) Excluded az-d via routing policy while we validated. 3) Deployed replacement NAT proxies in other AZs. 4) Flushed conntrack and drained old proxies. Customer impact limited and mostly transient.

Marta (support): Customers updated. No escalations to execs.

Priya (netops): Post-incident actions assigned: - disable automated route-table association rollouts for vpc-endpoint changes until a canary pass is in place (owner: Priya) - increase conntrack allocation for NAT proxies and add metric alert for conntrack utilization (owner: Nate) - add a guard in the Terraform pipeline to block ENI-based endpoint swaps without approval (owner: Sam).

Sam (oncall): Handing off to oncall-night for postmortem follow-through. Handoff note: all mitigation done, exclude-route still in place, will remove after postmortem validation.

incident-bot: Incident P-43921 resolved at 1739460402 by Sam (manual close).

Sam (oncall): Closing notes: timeframe ~40m. No data exfiltration or configuration drift beyond the route assoc. Will document timeline and add runbook entry for conntrack handling. :memo: :thumbsup:
